steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Earthquakes occur when stress builds up at plate boundaries and is suddenly released as seismic waves | Key Fact: The focus is the point underground where the earthquake originates; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above | Key Fact: Volcanoes form where magma reaches the surface: at divergent boundaries (fissure eruptions), subduction zones (explosive stratovolcanoes), and hotspots (shield volcanoes) | Key Fact: Effusive eruptions produce fluid basaltic lava (e.g. Iceland); explosive eruptions produce viscous andesitic/rhyolitic lava, ash and pyroclastic flows (e.g. Mt St Helens)

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from earthquakes &amp; volcanoes, and one past-paper question.
